title: CVE-2022-27778: curl removes wrong file on error
excerpt:
## Summary:
Curl command has a logic flaw that results in removal of a wrong file when combining  `--no-clobber` and `--remove-on-error` if the target file name exists and an error occurs.

## Steps To Reproduce:
  1. `echo "important file" > foo`
  2. `echo -ne "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\r\nContent-Length: 666\r\n\r\nHello\n" | nc -l -p 9999`
  3. `curl -m 3 --no-clobber --remove-on-error --output foo http://testserver.tld:9999/`
  4. `ls -l foo*`
  5. `cat foo.1`

`-m 3` is used here to simulate a denial of service of the connection performed by the attacker.

The bug appears to happen because the remote-on-error `unlink` is called without considering the no-clobber generated file name:
- no-clobber name generation; https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/3fd1d8df3a2497078d580f43c17311e6f58186a1/src/tool_cb_wrt.c#L88
- remove-on-error unlink: https://github.com/curl/curl/blob/f7f26077bc563375becdb2adbcd49eb9f28590f9/src/tool_operate.c#L598

## Impact

Removal of a file that was supposed not to be overwritten (data loss). Incomplete file left of disk when it should have been removed. This can lead to potential loss of integrity or availability.

For this attack to work the attacker of course would need to know a scenario where the victim is performing curl operation with  `--no-clobber` `--remove-on-error`  options.

summary: Curl removes a wrong file when using --no-clobber and --remove-on-error together, causing unintended data loss.

claims.text: curl removes the wrong file when combining --no-clobber and --remove-on-error if the target file name exists and an error occurs
claims.reasoning: The remove-on-error logic at lines 598-600 unlinks per->outfile, which is the original user-specified output filename. The no-clobber logic (tool_cb_wrt.c line 88 per deterministic checks) generates an alternative filename when the target exists but does not update per->outfile, so the wrong file is removed.

citations.note: unlink(per->outfile) called on error with rm_partial set

claims.text: the bug occurs in the remove-on-error unlink logic
claims.reasoning: The bug is in the remove-on-error unlink logic at lines 598-600 of tool_operate.c, which uses per->outfile (the original name) instead of the actual file written to when no-clobber renamed it.

citations.note: uses per->outfile for the filename to remove

claims.text: when a file with the same name already exists and an error happens during transfer
claims.reasoning: The trigger is an error during transfer (result != CURLE_OK) combined with --remove-on-error (config->rm_partial). The no-clobber condition (file exists) is handled in tool_cb_wrt.c line 88 per deterministic checks.

claims.text: removal of a file that was supposed not to be overwritten, leading to data loss
claims.reasoning: The original file (foo) is deleted despite --no-clobber, and the partial file (foo.1) is left behind despite --remove-on-error, causing both data loss and incomplete file retention.

citations.note: unlink removes per->outfile (original file protected by --no-clobber)
partial file (e.g., foo.1) remains on disk

claims.text: steps to reproduce involve creating a file, starting a server, and running curl with --no-clobber --remove-on-error
claims.reasoning: Reproduction steps are concrete and match the code path: create existing file, start server, run curl with --no-clobber --remove-on-error -m 3 to trigger timeout/error, observe wrong file removed.

key_reasons: tool_operate.c:598-600 unlinks per->outfile (original name) on error with --remove-on-error
tool_cb_wrt.c:88 (per deterministic checks) generates alternative name for --no-clobber but does not update per->outfile
Result: original file deleted (violates --no-clobber), partial file remains (violates --remove-on-error)
reply: Thank you for the detailed report. The code confirms the flaw: tool_operate.c:598-600 removes per->outfile (the original filename) on error, but --no-clobber writes to a generated name (e.g., foo.1) without updating per->outfile. This deletes the protected file and leaves the partial file. We'll fix the remove-on-error logic to unlink the actual written file.
